text.p: - Slovenian parliamentary president Janez Podobnik on Monday started a one-week official visit to the United States where he will also meet Slovenian emigrants.
- Real average wages of managers rose by 24 percent in 1996 while workers' wages rose only eight percent, representatives of trade unions said.
- The student organisation has collected 10,000 signatures for a petition against a plan by Slovenian insurance firms to hike car-insurance premiums by 35 percent for drivers under 25.
- January average gross wages fell 1.6 percent to 138,586 tolars ($901) compared to the previous month and rose 15.8 percent compared to January 1996.
- A fire began on Monday near the northern town of Jesenice, endangering some 25 hectares (62 acres) of forest. The risk of fires is high across the country after a long period without rain.
- Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler will meet Sir Arthur Watts, mediator in succession talks between former Yugoslav republics in Ljubljana on Tuesday.

- Representatives of Slovenian workers joined protests of Renault workers in Belgium against a plan to axe 6,000 jobs, expressing full sympathy with the protesters and saying the same could happen to them.
